newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico arrests two alleged drug cartel members.
newsitem.headline: Mexico arrests two alleged drug cartel members.

text.p: Mexican authorities have seized two alleged drug traffickers from the so-called Juarez Cartel, one of whom is wanted in the United States, Mexican state news agency Notimex reported late on Wednesday.

Citing a statement from the attorney-general's office, it said the two detainees were Jaime Gonzalez Gutierrez, who is wanted on drugs charges in the United States, and Jorge Varela Martinez, an alleged cross-border cocaine smuggler.
Both men had pseudonyms and aliases.

According to the attorney-general's office, both worked for Mexico's most powerful drug lord, Amado Carrillo Fuentes, known as "Lord of the Skies" because of his huge air shipments of cocaine from Colombia, via Mexico, to the United States.

Mexican police have stepped up their search for Carrillo Fuentes ahead of a visit to Mexico by U.S. President Bill Clinton next week, believeing him a prize catch to impress doubters in the United States that Mexico is tough on drug traffickers.

The report said both detained men sought to bribe their captors $100,000 to let them go, but they were turned down. They were taken to Mexico's maximum security prison Almoloya outside the capital, it said.
